program_understanding.program_purpose: The program reads an integer count from standard input, validates that it is a positive integer, then reads count integers from standard input and accumulates them into a 64-bit integer variable. It computes the arithmetic mean by performing a floating-point division of the sum by the count. Finally, it prints the mean formatted to two decimal places.
program_understanding.actual_behavior: The program reads an integer count from standard input, validates that it is a positive integer, then reads count integers from standard input and accumulates them into a 64-bit integer variable. It computes the arithmetic mean by performing a floating-point division of the sum by the count. Finally, it prints the mean formatted to two decimal places.
program_understanding.intended_behavior: The assignment requires computing the arithmetic mean of a set of signed integers without truncating fractional results. The program should read the number of elements, ensure the count is positive, read the values, sum them using a 64-bit accumulator, divide the sum by the count using floating-point arithmetic, and print the result with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
program_understanding.contract_alignment: The submitted source fully aligns with the assignment intent. It correctly reads input, accumulates values in a 64-bit integer, performs floating-point division, and outputs the result formatted to two decimal places.
program_understanding.algorithm_overview: The program uses a simple loop to accumulate input values into a long long variable, then performs a single division operation to compute the mean, followed by a formatted print statement.
